title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 5
paragraphs: For this reason he sent Morychides to Salamis. He came before the Council and delivered the words of Mardonius. Then one of the Councillors, Lykidas, expressed the opinion that it was better to accept the proposal Morychides had brought and refer it to the assembly of the people. This was the opinion he gave — whether because he had taken money from Mardonius, or because it was his own inclination. However the Athenians, both those of the Council and those outside, when they heard of it, were greatly indignant; they gathered around Lykidas and stoned him to death. The Hellespontian Morychides they dismissed unharmed. When there had arisen much uproar in Salamis about Lykidas, the Athenian women heard what was being done, and one passing the word to another and one bringing another along, they went of their own accord to Lykidas's house and stoned his wife and children to death.
